title: POC Weekly Sync - SDK tool/function calls & structured output - ZenHealth
summary: Weekly POC sync to review integration progress with Redwood SDK: function/tool calling, structured output mapping for clinical summary extraction, latency numbers from initial perf run, and security gating for VPC deployment. Action items: Redwood to share updated SDK sample with tool calling patterns, customer to run targeted benchmark on 512-token context and report perf, schedule infra call re: VPC/KMS.
next_steps: Redwood: share updated SDK sample with function-calling examples (Maya) - due 2026-09-04
ZenHealth: run perf test (512 token, 4 concurrency) and upload results to shared spreadsheet (Marcus) - due 2026-09-07
Schedule security deep-dive re: VPC, KMS, audit logs (Maya/Carlos + ZenHealth Sec) - target 2026-09-09
action_items: Maya Chen - send updated SDK repo link and sample code demonstrating tool+function calls and structured output parsing - due 2026-09-04
Carlos Ruiz - prepare perf checklist and recommended config for batching/kv cache for ZenHealth workload - due 2026-09-06
Marcus Green - run latency/cost perf tests and upload CSV to shared drive - due 2026-09-07
Priya Patel - confirm stakeholders for security deep dive and provide SSO/SAML contact - due 2026-09-05
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We planned 45 minutes, quick sync on the SDK integration, function calls, structured output. Priya, Marcus, Lina, you good?
[00:12] Priya (ZenHealth): Yes, good, thanks. We got a couple updates from the eng side and then Lina has results from the first perf run.
[00:20] Carlos (Redwood SE): Great, I'll jump into the function-calling details after Maya covers the updated SDK bits.
[00:28] Marcus (ZenHealth): Quick note, we're on the 0.9.1 branch of your SDK sample, has the tool-calling example but not the structured output mapping yet.
[00:36] Maya: Right, that's what we wanted to show\u0004there's a new sample that wires tool and function calls together and returns a JSON schema you can map to your clinical summary object. We'll share the link in a sec.
[00:46] Lina (ZenHealth): I ran a perf pass earlier today, 100 requests, 256 token responses, single model variant, average latency was 210ms per token at our edge region, which is promising but our SLA target is 150ms per token.
[01:02] Carlos: Okay two quick calls out \u0004 first, the difference may be due to batching and KV cache settings; second, what sequence length distribution do your requests usually have?
[01:12] Priya: Typical summaries are 200-600 tokens, sometimes 1k for full visit notes. But for the pilot we're focusing 200-400 tokens.
[01:22] Marcus: Also, we're doing some pre- and post-processing on the client side which might add 30-40ms.
[01:30] Maya: Cool. On the SDK side, we've added a functional example that uses the SDK's tool-calling primitives. It exposes an API like: redwood.generate({model:..., functions:[...], call: 'auto'}), and returns either text or a structured function call payload you can parse. The sample uses a 'extract_clinical_summary' function schema.
[01:52] Carlos: Important practical note \u0004 the SDK will sometimes return 'function_call' events in streaming mode, and you'll see partial payloads. Our sample shows how to buffer and assemble the JSON safely; we included heuristics for bracket-matching because transcriptions often cut off.
[02:10] Lina: Nice. We had an issue where the parser crashed when the model emitted single quotes in the JSON, and our existing parser assumed double quotes only.
[02:18] Maya: Ugh, yes that's a classic transcribe artifact. The sample parser includes normalization steps: convert smart quotes, ensure keys are quoted, fallback to a regex extractor. Not perfect but reduces crashes.
[02:30] Marcus: On structured output mapping: our object model is Patient->Visit->Summaries (array). We need a strict schema so downstream systems don't break. Can Redwood enforce schema validation on the model output side?
[02:44] Carlos: We don't modify the model output but we provide structured-output helpers. Two options: 1) Use function calling with a strict JSON Schema \u0004 that nudges the model to return the object format; 2) Post-validate with the SDK helper that returns 'valid:true/false' plus a sanitized payload. For pilot I'd recommend function calling plus schema validation on your end.
[03:05] Priya: Sounds good. For compliance we'd like to log any schema mismatches to audit logs. Is that available?
[03:12] Maya: Yes, Dedicated and Private plans can push detailed audit logs. For hosted we log higher-level traces; we can also push redacted transcripts on request. We'll share the doc.
[03:24] Carlos: Also, if you plan to go Private with VPC and KMS, the Private deployment gives you application-level key control and full audit logs. For the pilot we can simulate by enabling request-level masking and storing trace ids.
[03:39] Lina: Back to perf \u0004 we noticed latency spikes at 40 concurrent requests. Any recommended batching config?
[03:46] Carlos: Two levers: reduce max_batch_wait_ms if you need lower tail latency, but that impacts throughput. Also, prefix/KV cache helps a lot if you have repeated context. For medical summaries the visit header is often repeated across requests so caching the KV for the first 128 tokens can save cycles.
[04:05] Marcus: How about quantized model variants? We tried a 4-bit variant and saw quality deltas on entity extraction.
[04:13] Maya: Yep, quantization tradeoffs exist. Our Optimize team runs quality monitors; for extraction-heavy tasks we often recommend FP16 or 8-bit quant with eval benchmarks. We can recommend a quantization profile tuned for NER/medical extraction.
[04:29] Priya: Security question \u0004 we need SSO and SAML for the console, RBAC, and SAML provisioning for service accounts. Is that supported?
[04:38] Maya: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported for Enterprise plans; RBAC roles map to console and API tokens. For Private you'll get customer-managed IdP integration.
[04:48] Carlos: Also note the API tokens can be rotated via KMS in Private deployments; hosted supports integration with customer KMS for key wrapping in some setups. We'll detail options in the security doc.
[04:59] Lina: One more thing \u0004 the function call schema: can we define nested arrays and optional keys? Our Summary object needs notes[], diagnoses[], and optional follow_up boolean.
[05:09] Carlos: JSON Schema supports required/optional fields and nested arrays. The function-calling schema we suggest will include types and maxLength for strings to prevent runaway tokens. We recommend marking follow_up optional.
[05:23] Marcus: Good. On the SDK, how do we handle retries for partial function-call streams? We saw duplicated outputs after a client-side retry.
[05:31] Maya: The SDK includes idempotency keys and a stream-reconnect helper. If you retry, include the original idempotency key and the server will reconcile partial outputs where possible. For function calls, we recommend atomic commit: only ack when JSON parsed and validated.
[05:48] Priya: That's helpful. Lina, can you walk us through today's perf run details?
[05:54] Lina: Sure. Test harness: 100 requests, 256 tokens target, concurrency 8, model variant 'redwood-7b-0' (hosted). Average E2E latency 1.2s, tokenization overhead ~120ms, per-token generation average 210ms as mentioned. P95 was 2.6s, spikes aligned with concurrency bursts.
[06:16] Carlos: Thanks. Can you also share the histogram and the raw timings? That helps us tune queue/batching parameters.
[06:23] Marcus: Uploaded to the shared drive: perf_20260902.csv, also the harness config in the repo.
[06:29] Maya: We'll review and propose config changes: reduce max_batch_size, tweak batch timeout, and recommend KV cache placements. Also propose trying the 'dedicated' instance pilot \u0004 even a small dedicated endpoint shifts tail latency down for predictable workloads.
[06:45] Priya: Cost question \u0004 dedicated will be more expensive. What's the rough delta?
[06:50] Maya: Depends on commitment. For small dedicated pool it's higher fixed cost but lower per-token for heavy sustained traffic. We can run a cost model once we have your projected qps and concurrency.
[07:02] Marcus: Pricing sheet would be great \u0004 include burst pricing and overage.
[07:06] Maya: Will send.
[07:08] Carlos: A couple of gotchas: when using function calling with streaming, be careful with partial JSON flushes \u0004 we recommend finalization markers in the stream so the SDK can detect completion. The sample includes an example with '_end_of_function_call': true.
[07:27] Lina: Ha, that will save us lots of parser headaches.
[07:30] Priya: For the security deep dive, I'll invite our Head of Security, Aaron. He needs SOC2 evidence, pen-test report, and network topology for Private.
[07:39] Maya: We'll prepare SOC2 cert, pen-test summary, and sample network diagram. For Private deployments we can supply an architecture diagram showing VPC peering and on-prem connectors.
[07:50] Marcus: Anything else on structured output? We want a small set of unit tests that validate model outputs against schema. Can you share testing harness?
[07:58] Carlos: Yes, we have a small validation harness used by our QA \u0004 schema fuzzing and canonicalization steps. We'll send it and show how to plug it into your CI.
[08:07] Maya: Quick recap of next steps: 1) Redwood share updated SDK examples and parser (Maya), 2) Carlos to propose batching/KV config and perf checklist, 3) ZenHealth to run the 512-token perf and upload results, 4) schedule security deep-dive.
[08:25] Priya: Agreed. One ask: can we get a short recording of the function-calling sample workflow for the team? A 10-minute screen share would be ideal.
[08:33] Maya: Yes we can record a short demo. I'll schedule for next week.
[08:36] Marcus: Thanks, that would be super helpful.
[08:39] Lina: One small note \u0004 can the SDK sample include node + python examples? We run both stacks.
[08:44] Maya: Yes both. We'll include node and python snippets and a dockerized example for the harness.
[08:50] Priya: Great. If nothing else, let's close.
[08:52] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the links and proposed dates.
[08:56] Meeting end.
